page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-8-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB per core, and includes a single 137 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

Benchmark evaluations show average performance across most standard compute workloads, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1867.0 and a multi-core score of 7017.0. The server demonstrates strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.27 GB/sec and top-tier text processing capabilities, scoring 2961.0 in Geekbench text processing. However, memory subsystem limitations are evident; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 668.21 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to a weak 29.93 GB/sec, and the overall Passmark memory score is categorized as weak.

This server configuration is suitable for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and lightweight database operations, supported by its local NVMe SSD and average Passmark database score of 3723.97. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions enables efficient small-scale machine learning tasks, as reflected in the strong text generation speed of 277.66 tokens/sec for a 135M parameter LLM. The primary tradeoff is the weak uncached memory bandwidth, which may limit performance in memory-intensive applications or large-dataset processing that exceeds the 504 MB L3 cache.
